sermon.title: The Spirit of Fear
sermon.speaker: Guest speaker (unnamed)
sermon.summary: A Vine Cluster Church message reading 2 Timothy 1:7 in context: because God has given power, love and a sound mind, don’t be ashamed of the testimony of the Lord. Paul’s testimony before Agrippa shows the chief of sinners turned from darkness to light and preaching repentance. 1 Corinthians 6 lists who will not inherit the kingdom, yet “such were some of you”—Christ washes and changes.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: “some sawn in half… torn by beasts” attributed to Paul (Hebrews 11:37); Matthew 23:15 paraphrased as Jesus saying “two times a child of hell”; the claim that the word for forgiveness means liberty/release. Unverified statistics as spoken (30:24–33:00): 1 in 5 pregnancies aborted, 1 in 10 children abused, 43% fatherless, 90% of homeless/runaways, 80% of rapists, 71% of pregnant teens and dropouts, 85% of youth in prison from fatherless homes. Sensitive: misuse of the verse to excuse child abuse (3:15). Private details (the speaker’s wife’s name and employer) appear only in the transcript.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.

faqs.question: What does “spirit of fear” mean?
faqs.answer: Cowardice or timidity that makes you back down.

faqs.question: Can you take one verse alone?
faqs.answer: No—you have to read the whole thing in context.

faqs.question: What does “therefore” in 2 Timothy 1:8 mean?
faqs.answer: For this reason—because God has given power, love and a sound mind, don’t be ashamed.

faqs.question: Is attacking God’s people attacking Jesus?
faqs.answer: Yes—we are the body of Christ.

faqs.question: Is everyone called to be a minister?
faqs.answer: No, but all are called to repent and follow Jesus.

faqs.question: Do we judge people?
faqs.answer: The Bible judges; we go by what Jesus says.

faqs.question: Can people be changed from these sins?
faqs.answer: Yes—with Christ all things are possible.

faqs.question: What might standing for Christ cost today?
Why focus on getting Scripture out?
faqs.answer: When parents turn and transform, they care for their children.
